submission.prompt_text: Some people think that governments should spend money on improving public transport rather than building new roads. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
submission.essay_text:
Nowadays transport is very important problem in many country. Some people think goverment should spend money for public transport not for build new road. I am agree with this opinion in some way but not all.

Firstly, public transport is good for people. Because many people dont have car and they need bus and train to go work and school. If the bus is more better, people will use it more and the traffic will be less. In my city the bus is always late and very crowd so people dont like to take it. Also the train is too expensive for student. So goverment should make it cheap and more fast.

Secondly, new road is also important. Because the city is grow and more people buy car every year. If there is no new road the traffic jam will be very bad and people waste a lot of time. For example my father drive to work everyday and he spend two hour in the road. This is very bad for him and for the economy also.

But I think public transport is more important than road. Because the road make more car and more pollution. The public transport can carry many people in one time and it is good for enviroment. Also if more people take bus, the city will be more quiet and the air will be more clean, so everybody can be more healthy and happy.

In conclusion, I think goverment should spend more money for public transport but also build some road when it is necessary. Both is important for the people and the country develop.

submission.prompt_text: Some people think that governments should spend money on improving public transport rather than building new roads. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
submission.essay_text:
In many cities, traffic congestion has become a serious problem, and governments must decide how to use limited budgets. Some people argue that money should go to public transport instead of new roads. I mostly agree with this view, although I believe some road building is still necessary.

The main reason to invest in public transport is that it can move a large number of people efficiently. A single train can carry hundreds of passengers, while the same number of people would need hundreds of cars. If buses and trains are frequent, cheap and reliable, many drivers will choose them, which will reduce traffic jams. For example, after my city opened a new metro line, the main road to the city centre became much less crowded during rush hour.

Another advantage is the environment. Cars produce a lot of air pollution and carbon emissions, which are harmful to people's health and contribute to climate change. Public transport produces less pollution per passenger, so it is a more sustainable option in the long term.

On the other hand, new roads are sometimes needed. In rural areas, there are not enough passengers to make train lines profitable, so people depend on cars. Also, goods are mostly transported by trucks, and poor roads can slow down the economy.

In conclusion, I agree that governments should give priority to public transport because it is more efficient and better for the environment. However, they should still build roads in places where public transport is not practical.

criteria.label: Task Response
criteria.summary: 全文紧扣题目：明确表态“主要支持公共交通，但保留必要的道路建设”，并在主体段分别用效率、环境两条理由支撑，第四段用乡村与货运说明例外，结尾重申同一立场且不遗漏例外，属于有条件的立场，前后一致。每个论点都给出了因果解释或个人实例，论证完整度达到7分要求；不足之处是论证深度偏浅、篇幅刚过250词，个别论断（货运主要靠卡车）略显笼统。

strengths.quote: I mostly agree with this view, although I believe some road building is still necessary.
strengths.comment: 开篇即给出清晰且有条件限定的立场，为后文的分层论证定下框架。

strengths.quote: If buses and trains are frequent, cheap and reliable, many drivers will choose them, which will reduce traffic jams.
strengths.comment: 用条件句加结果从句把“投资公交→吸引私家车主→缓解拥堵”的因果链讲清楚，是有效的论证而非空泛断言。

strengths.quote: after my city opened a new metro line, the main road to the city centre became much less crowded
strengths.comment: 用一个具体（可合理视为假设性）的地方实例支撑前面的效率论点，例子紧贴论点，无需额外总结句即已扣题。

issues.quote: Also, goods are mostly transported by trucks, and poor roads can slow down the economy.
issues.comment: “most goods are transported by trucks”是一个未加限定的全局性断言，读者可能质疑其适用范围，属于轻度过度概括，削弱了让步段的说服力。
issues.suggestion: 改成有保留的表述，如 “in many countries a large share of freight is moved by truck, so poor roads can slow the economy”，使论断更稳妥。

issues.quote: Public transport produces less pollution per passenger, so it is a more sustainable option in the long term.
issues.comment: 环境段只有两句话的推理，没有具体化（例如按人均排放比较或举一个城市空气改善的情形），论证展开明显弱于第二段，使整体论证深度不均衡。
issues.suggestion: 补一句比较或后果，如 “because a full bus carries about forty times as many people as a car using only a fraction of the fuel per person”，让环境论点同样“落地”。

criteria.label: Coherence & Cohesion
criteria.summary: 五段结构清晰：引入—理由一—理由二—让步—结论，信息推进自然，读者能顺畅跟随论证路线。指代（this view、it、they）基本准确，连接词使用得当；但 “The main reason / Another advantage / On the other hand / In conclusion” 属于较公式化的排列，段落之间更接近“条目罗列”而非层层递进。

strengths.quote: On the other hand, new roads are sometimes needed.
strengths.comment: 用明确的转折信号词开启让步段，使“有限度同意”的结构一目了然。

strengths.quote: In conclusion, I agree that governments should give priority to public transport
strengths.comment: 结尾用总结信号词回收全文立场，并随后补出例外，收束干净。

strengths.quote: The main reason to invest in public transport is that it can move a large number of people efficiently.
strengths.comment: 主题句直接点明本段功能，段落主旨清晰，便于评分者快速识别论证结构。

issues.quote: Another advantage is the environment.
issues.comment: 段落以“Another advantage is…”这种模板化短语开头，且该段仅两句、缺少例证或展开，与前后段的信息密度落差明显，读起来像清单而非连贯论证。
issues.suggestion: 改为带逻辑关系的主题句，如 “Investment in public transport also brings environmental benefits that roads cannot match.”，并在段内加一句展开或比较，使段落自然承接上一段。

criteria.label: Lexical Resource
criteria.summary: 词汇整体准确、搭配自然（traffic congestion, carbon emissions, a more sustainable option, make train lines profitable），能支撑话题表达，拼写与词形无错。但范围有限，多为常见词与中频话题词，缺少较不常见或更精确的表达，个别处用词偏口语（a lot of, much less crowded），因此未达到7分所需的灵活与精确度。

strengths.quote: Cars produce a lot of air pollution and carbon emissions, which are harmful to people's health and contribute to climate change.
strengths.comment: 准确使用话题词组与搭配（carbon emissions, contribute to climate change），显示对环保类词汇的掌握。

strengths.quote: In rural areas, there are not enough passengers to make train lines profitable
strengths.comment: “make … profitable”搭配准确，用经济可行性来解释例外，表达简洁到位。

issues.quote: the main road to the city centre became much less crowded during rush hour
issues.comment: 表达正确但词汇层次偏基础（much less crowded），属于口语化描述，未体现学术写作所需的精确度。
issues.suggestion: 可改为 “traffic on the main artery into the city centre dropped noticeably during peak hours”，用 artery、peak hours 等更精确的表达。

issues.quote: Cars produce a lot of air pollution
issues.comment: “a lot of” 属口语化量词，在学术语域中显得不够正式、也不够精确。
issues.suggestion: 改为 “emit large quantities of / substantial amounts of air pollution”。

criteria.label: Grammatical Range & Accuracy
criteria.summary: 语法准确性很高，全文基本无可辨认的错误，标点使用规范。句式包含条件状语从句、非限制性定语从句、while 引导的对比以及 where 引导的定语从句，具备一定复杂结构；但句型种类相对集中，多数句子采用“简单陈述＋which/so 结果”的模式，变化的丰富度还不足以支撑更高分数。

strengths.quote: A single train can carry hundreds of passengers, while the same number of people would need hundreds of cars.
strengths.comment: 用 while 构成清晰对比，并以数量关系加强论点，属于有效且准确的复杂句。

strengths.quote: they should still build roads in places where public transport is not practical
strengths.comment: where 引导的定语从句使用准确，把例外的范围限定清楚，语法与意义配合良好。

issues.quote: Cars produce a lot of air pollution and carbon emissions, which are harmful to people's health
issues.comment: “which” 非限制性定语从句在全文反复出现，句式手段较为单一，复杂结构的种类不够多样。
issues.suggestion: 可交替使用分词结构或让步从句，如 “Cars emit substantial pollution, harming people's health and driving climate change” 或 “Although public transport requires heavy initial spending, it cuts long-term costs”。

result.overall_comment: 这是一篇结构规范、语言准确、立场清晰的作文，稳定在7分左右。最大优势是“有条件的立场”处理得当：主张优先投资公共交通，同时用乡村与货运的实际需要界定例外，且结论回到同一立场，不出现自相矛盾；主体段也都有因果解释或实例，而非空喊口号。主要提升空间在于论证的厚度与词汇的精度：环境段过于单薄，个别论断（货运主要靠卡车）缺少限定；词汇以常见话题词为主，兼有 a lot of 这类口语表达；句式虽无错误，但“which/so”式结构反复出现，复杂句种类偏单一。若把环境段扩充到与效率段相当的篇幅，并在让步段的断言前加限定语，同时用更精确的动词和名词替换基础表达，整体有望向7.5迈进。
priorities: 扩充第三段（环境）论证：加入人均排放比较或一个具体后果，使两条理由分量相当。
给第四段的全局性断言加限定语（如 in many countries / a large proportion of freight），避免过度概括。
提升词汇精度：用 emit substantial pollution、peak hours、artery 等替代 a lot of、much less crowded 等基础表达。
丰富句式种类：减少 which 非限制性定语从句的重复，穿插分词结构、让步从句与名词化表达。
避免模板化的段落开头（Another advantage is…），让主题句携带逻辑关系，使段落之间呈现递进而非罗列。

position.quote: I mostly agree with this view, although I believe some road building is still necessary.
position.comment: 这是一个有限度但明确的立场：资金以公共交通为主，道路建设在必要时保留。第四段的让步正是在界定这一立场的适用范围，结论也重复了同样的限定，全文不存在自相矛盾的表述。

paragraphs.comment: 交代背景并给出有条件的立场，明确全文方向。

paragraphs.main_point: The main reason to invest in public transport is that it can move a large number of people efficiently.
paragraphs.comment: 给出效率理由，并通过条件推理与地方实例完成论证，直接服务于“优先投资公交”的立场。

paragraphs.comment: 从环境角度补充理由，用“人均污染更低”说明公交更可持续，论点与立场一致；展开较简略但并非无理由。

paragraphs.main_point: On the other hand, new roads are sometimes needed.

paragraphs.main_point: In conclusion, I agree that governments should give priority to public transport because it is more efficient and better for the environment.
paragraphs.comment: 总结两条主要理由并重申优先投资公交，同时保留“不实际的地方仍需修路”的例外，与首段立场完全一致。

submission.prompt_text: Some people think that governments should spend money on improving public transport rather than building new roads. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
submission.essay_text:
As urban populations grow, governments face a difficult choice about where to direct transport spending. While some advocate building more roads to ease congestion, I largely agree that public transport deserves the greater share of investment, because it addresses the causes of traffic problems rather than merely their symptoms.

The strongest argument for prioritising public transport is efficiency. Roads are an inherently limited resource: a lane of motorway can carry only a fixed number of private vehicles per hour, whereas a well-run rail or bus rapid transit line can move many times that number of people in the same space. Moreover, there is considerable evidence that new roads tend to fill up quickly, as cheaper and faster journeys encourage more people to drive. Expanding road networks may therefore offer only temporary relief before congestion returns.

Public transport also brings wider social and environmental benefits. It gives affordable mobility to those who cannot drive, such as students, the elderly and lower-income workers, thereby widening their access to jobs and services. At the same time, shifting journeys from cars to trains and buses reduces both air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions, which is increasingly important as cities attempt to meet climate targets.

Nevertheless, it would be unrealistic to stop road building altogether. In sparsely populated regions, buses and trains are rarely viable, and freight still relies heavily on trucks. Targeted road improvements, such as bypasses around congested towns, can therefore remain a sensible use of funds.

In conclusion, although some road investment is still justified, governments should concentrate their spending on public transport, since it offers a more lasting solution to congestion while also delivering social and environmental gains.

submission.prompt_text: Some people think that governments should spend money on improving public transport rather than building new roads. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
submission.essay_text:
How a government allocates its transport budget shapes not only how quickly people travel, but also the kind of cities they live in. Although there is an intuitive appeal to building new roads whenever traffic worsens, I am convinced that investment should be weighted decisively towards public transport, with road construction reserved for cases where no realistic alternative exists.

The case for new roads rests largely on the assumption that congestion is a shortage of capacity. Yet experience from many large cities suggests otherwise: widening a motorway lowers the cost of driving, which in turn draws additional traffic until the new lanes are as clogged as the old ones. This phenomenon, often described as induced demand, means that road building can become an expensive treadmill. Public transport, by contrast, increases the number of people a corridor can carry without a proportional increase in the space consumed, and a single metro line can relieve pressure on an entire network of streets.

Equally important are the distributional consequences. Road spending disproportionately benefits those who own cars, whereas frequent and affordable buses and trains extend opportunity to people who cannot or prefer not to drive. Well-designed transit also allows denser, more walkable neighbourhoods to develop around stations, reducing the distances people need to travel in the first place, and it cuts emissions at a time when the transport sector remains one of the most stubborn sources of carbon.

That said, a blanket refusal to build roads would be misguided. Rural communities and freight logistics depend on reliable highways, and in such contexts targeted upgrades may represent genuine value for money.

On balance, therefore, public transport should receive the lion's share of funding, because it tackles congestion at its root and produces broader social and environmental returns that new roads rarely match.

submission.essay_text:
Online learning has grown rapidly over the past decade, and many people now believe that it will eventually replace traditional classrooms. In my view, although online courses offer clear advantages, face-to-face education will remain essential.

The most obvious benefit of online learning is flexibility. Students can watch lectures at any time and study at their own pace, which is especially useful for adults who work full-time or have family responsibilities. Online courses can also reach learners in remote areas who would otherwise have no access to good teachers. In addition, digital materials can be updated quickly, and learners can replay difficult explanations as many times as they need, which is impossible in a traditional lecture. For many people, these features make online study cheaper and more convenient than attending a college in person.

However, classroom learning provides things that are difficult to replicate on a screen. Teachers can notice immediately when a student is confused and adapt their explanations. Students also develop social skills by working together, discussing ideas and building friendships, which are an important part of education, particularly for children.

Furthermore, many learners find it hard to stay motivated without the structure of a timetable and the presence of classmates. Completion rates for many free online courses are notoriously low, which suggests that self-discipline is a serious obstacle.

In conclusion, online learning is a valuable supplement that makes education more accessible and flexible, but it is unlikely to replace traditional classrooms, which offer interaction, support and motivation that technology cannot fully provide.

submission.prompt_text: The bar chart below shows the percentage of households that owned a car in four countries in 2000 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
submission.essay_text:
The bar chart compares the proportion of households with a car in four countries in 2000 and 2020.

Overall, car ownership increased in all four countries over the period, although the size of the rise varied considerably. Country A had the highest level of ownership in both years, while Country D remained the lowest.

In 2000, around 70% of households in Country A owned a car, compared with roughly 55% in Country B and about 40% in Country C. Country D had by far the lowest figure, at only 15%.

By 2020, the percentage in Country A had risen slightly to about 75%, and Country B had grown to approximately 65%. The most dramatic change was seen in Country C, where ownership almost doubled to nearly 80%, overtaking Country A. Country D also experienced significant growth, reaching around 35%, but it was still well behind the other three countries.

In summary, while every country saw an increase, the growth was particularly striking in Country C and much more modest in Country A.

criteria.label: Coherence & Cohesion
criteria.summary: 文章按「概述—2000年—2020年—总结」推进，信息安排清楚，读者能顺畅跟住行文逻辑；指代（the other three countries、it）与连接手段基本有效。但172词被拆成五个自然段，段落切分偏碎，且最后一段几乎是概述的重复，衔接方式也较模板化（In 2000 / By 2020 / In summary），因此未达到7.0所需的自然、灵活的行文衔接。

strengths.quote: Overall, car ownership increased in all four countries over the period
strengths.comment: 第二段给出清晰的总体趋势概述，位置恰当、概括到位，为后文数据段提供了统摄。

strengths.quote: In 2000, around 70% of households in Country A owned a car
strengths.comment: 以时间状语开段，配合 the most dramatic change、also、but 等标记，段落内部推进方向明确，读者容易定位信息。

issues.quote: In summary, while every country saw an increase, the growth was particularly striking in Country C
issues.comment: 结尾段重复了第二段概述已表达的内容（全部上升＋C国涨幅最大），对Task 1而言是冗余，且让五段结构显得松散。
issues.suggestion: 删除该总结段，或将其压缩为一句并入概述段，例如在概述末补充 "with Country C showing the steepest rise."，把篇幅留给数据描述。

issues.quote: By 2020, the percentage in Country A had risen slightly
issues.comment: 段落与句子的起头方式高度模式化（In 2000 / By 2020 / In summary），衔接手段种类偏窄，读来有清单感。
issues.suggestion: 改用更灵活的衔接，如 "Twenty years later, ..."、"Turning to 2020, ..."、"The same period saw ..."，或在段内用 "whereas"、"by contrast" 组织对比。

criteria.label: Lexical Resource
criteria.summary: 词汇有一定变化，能用 by far the lowest figure、almost doubled、overtaking、particularly striking、much more modest 等较地道的表达，搭配总体准确，拼写无误。不足之处在于部分表达仍偏常规，且描述「上升」的词族（increase / rise / grow / growth）在同一篇中反复出现，个别动词与百分比的搭配不够精确。

strengths.quote: although the size of the rise varied considerably
strengths.comment: the size of the rise varied considerably 属较自然的抽象化表达，避免了逐条罗列数字，体现了一定的词汇掌控力。

strengths.quote: Country D had by far the lowest figure, at only 15%
strengths.comment: by far 与 at only 15% 搭配得当，语气与程度判断准确，是Task 1中较常见的得分词组。

issues.quote: and Country B had grown to approximately 65%
issues.comment: 用 grow 描述百分比数据不够精确，且与前一分句的 had risen 形成同义重复，语感上略显生硬。
issues.suggestion: 改为 "and the figure for Country B had climbed to approximately 65%"，或 "while Country B rose to approximately 65%"。

issues.quote: Country D also experienced significant growth
issues.comment: growth 与全文多处 increase / rise / risen 语义重叠，描述变化的词汇略显单一。
issues.suggestion: 可替换为 "Country D also saw a marked upturn" 或 "recorded a steady climb"，以增加词族多样性。

criteria.label: Grammatical Range & Accuracy
criteria.summary: 全文句式准确度很高，基本没有影响理解的语法错误；使用了定语从句（where ownership almost doubled）、分词状语（reaching around 35%、overtaking Country A）、比较结构与让步状语从句（although the size of the rise varied considerably）。错误少而轻微，主要是个别并列句省略主语造成的主语不一致，以及复杂句式的种类仍可再丰富。

strengths.quote: where ownership almost doubled to nearly 80%, overtaking Country A
strengths.comment: 定语从句＋现在分词状语叠加，两个信息点在一句内自然衔接，句法控制力好。

strengths.quote: reaching around 35%, but it was still well behind the other three countries
strengths.comment: 分词短语补充数据、转折分句给出比较判断，句子长短有变化，标点使用规范。

issues.quote: and Country B had grown to approximately 65%
issues.comment: 前一分句主语是 the percentage，本分句主语却变成 Country B，并列结构中省略不当，造成主语不一致。
issues.suggestion: 补出主语："and the figure for Country B had grown to approximately 65%"。

result.overall_comment: 语言层面这是一篇相当扎实的Task 1：概述清晰，数据描述按年份组织，句子准确度高，几乎没有影响理解的语法错误，词汇也能用到 by far、overtaking、striking 等较地道的表达。主要短板在组织与衔接：172词拆成五段偏碎，结尾段重复概述，段首句式（In 2000 / By 2020 / In summary）显得模板化；描述变化的词族略单一，个别搭配（had grown to a percentage）不够精确；另有一处并列句主语不一致。改进后，连贯与词汇都具备上探7.0的空间。
priorities: 删除或压缩结尾的总结段，避免与概述重复；把五个自然段合并为四段（引言＋概述＋两个数据段），使结构更紧凑。
丰富段落与句子的衔接方式，减少 In 2000 / By 2020 / In summary 这类模式化开头，改用 Twenty years later、Turning to 2020、by contrast 等。
扩充描述变化的词族，交替使用 rise、climb、grow、increase、upturn 等，避免同一语义反复出现。
注意并列句中的主语一致性，该补出主语时不要省略（the figure for Country B）。
检查概述与后文数据描述之间是否自洽，避免概述中的排名判断与数据段的结论相互矛盾。

consistency_issues.quote: Country A had the highest level of ownership in both years, while Country D remained the lowest
consistency_issues.comment: 2000年A确为最高、D最低；但2020年文中给出C国 nearly 80%，高于A国的约75%，因此“A在两年中都最高”与本文自身数据矛盾，也与后文 overtaking Country A 自相冲突。D在两年中最低这一点成立。
